subject: Fwd: Hosted vs Dedicated - latency/throughput follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finlytics.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted vs Dedicated - latency/throughput follow-up

Alex -- thanks for the call earlier. Quick recap and next steps from our side: 

Summary of what you shared:
- Primary application: real-time document classification and entity extraction embedded in your analyst UI.
- Latency target: p95 end-to-end under ~120ms for single-call inference.
- Expected traffic: steady-state ~200 req/s, with nightly batch spikes up to ~1,000 req/s for backfill jobs.
- Typical token usage: ~120 input tokens, ~40 output tokens per call.
- Data sensitivity: contains customer PII; you mentioned SOC2 + encryption at rest are important.

Initial recommendation:
- Hosted API: fastest time-to-value, simple integration. Works well if you can tolerate occasional variability during large spikes and don't need guaranteed dedicated throughput.
- Dedicated capacity: recommended if you need predictable sustained throughput and stricter latency SLOs. With Dedicated we can reserve GPU pools and set autoscale/burst policies to handle your peaks while keeping consistent p95.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): likely unnecessary unless procurement or compliance requires customer-managed networking; we can discuss if that becomes a hard requirement.

Questions / data we need to finalize recommendation and sizing:
1) Can you confirm the % of requests that need to hit the real-time path vs batch? (estimate)
2) Do you have a hard SLA requirement (e.g., p95 < 100ms) or a preferred target?
3) Any constraints around tokenization/model family (do you need a specific model or are open-model candidates acceptable)?

Next steps:
- If you confirm the traffic breakdown and SLA, we'll run a sizing exercise and share a Dedicated sizing + pricing worksheet (I'll loop in Vivek for the technical sizing).
- Proposed follow-up: 30-min technical deep-dive this week -- Vivek can walk through kernel-level optimizations and expected p95 for candidate models.

I've attached an initial pricing worksheet for a Dedicated configuration and a draft MAP we typically use for deals this size.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

Attachments: RWI-dedicated-pricing.pdf, MAP-Finlytics-v1.xlsx

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finlytics.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Singh <priya.singh@finlytics.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 15 Jul 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted vs Dedicated - latency/throughput follow-up

Thanks Marissa -- good recap and appreciate the worksheet. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Traffic split: ~90% real-time UI calls, ~10% nightly backfill. The backfill can be queued over a 3-4 hour window but peak TPS can reach ~1,000 for short bursts.
- Latency: our product team is targeting p95 <= 120ms for the UI. Anything above that starts to feel sluggish to users.
- Model: we're open to Redwood-curated open models. We'd like an assessment of trade-offs between using a smaller quantized model (cheaper, faster) vs a larger one for quality.
- Compliance: SOC2 + AES-256 at rest is required. We also need to confirm access logs for audit.

Procurement note: Priya (cc) will start the procurement process once we get the pricing cushion for Dedicated vs Hosted. At a high level, Finlytics would prefer Dedicated if the cost delta is justified by predictable p95. Please include an estimate for both sustained (200 req/s) and burst capacity to 1,000 req/s.

Happy to do the technical deep-dive Friday morning (your timezone).

--Alex
Alex Johnson
Product Lead, Finlytics
alex.johnson@finlytics.com

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 15 Jul 2026 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted vs Dedicated - latency/throughput follow-up (internal sizing notes)

Internal notes / sizing draft for Finlytics:

Assumptions based on Alex's numbers: 200 steady qps, p95 target 120ms, spikes to 1,000 qps for short bursts. Token profile ~160 tokens per call total.

- Candidate model family: 7B quantized variant (good balance) and 13B quantized (higher quality, ~1.5x latency).
- Estimated Dedicated pool sizing:
  * 7B quantized: 3 x A100-like GPUs with autoscale to 6 for burst smoothing (sustained cost lower, expected p95 ~70-90ms).
  * 13B quantized: 4 x A100-like GPUs with autoscale to 8 (higher cost, p95 ~110-140ms depending on kernel).
- Hosted viability: Hosted can hit target often but p95 variability during noisy neighbors is a risk. If Finlytics cannot tolerate p95 regressions during other tenant spikes, Dedicated is the safer option.
- Security: SOC2 + KMS-integrated disk encryption available for Dedicated and Private. Access logs + audit trail available via Console (we can export to your SIEM).

Attachments I'm adding: RWI-dedicated-pricing.pdf (breakdown by GPU profile), MAP-Finlytics-v1.xlsx (commercial playbook).

Recommended next steps for the customer meeting:
1) Present the two candidate configs (7B vs 13B) with expected p95 and cost delta.
2) Offer a 2-week Dedicated pilot with limited commit to validate p95 under real traffic.
3) Schedule the technical deep-dive Friday (30 min) to walk model trade-offs and autoscale behavior.

I'll prepare a short slide with latency/throughput expectations for both configs before Friday.

-Vivek
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
